tools.name: search_endpoints
tools.description: Find Perceptlayer endpoints for a website or kind of data. The catalogue has 2454 endpoints across 397 sources, so search before calling. Query with the site and the data you want, e.g. "amazon product reviews", "airbnb listing", "linkedin company", "google maps places", "zillow property". Returns c

tools.name: get_endpoint
tools.description: Get the full parameter list for one endpoint: each parameter's name, type, whether it is required, allowed values and limits, plus an example set of parameters, the credit cost and tier. Call this before call_endpoint unless you already know the parameters. Free; no API key needed.

tools.name: call_endpoint
tools.description: Run one endpoint and return its JSON response. Spends the call's credits from the user's balance on success only; failed calls are free. Pass parameters exactly as get_endpoint lists them (array parameters as JSON arrays). The result reports credits used and remaining. Errors come back with a code:

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_endpoints" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.detail: Description of "call_endpoint" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
